stories.Headline: Additional Information on the Ehrmann Family Increasing Its Equity Stake in Artprice by Artmarket as Part of Artprice's "AI-First" Transformation
stories.Summary:
The Ehrmann family, which controls Artmarket.com through Groupe Serveur, is increasing its equity stake in the company as part of Artprice's transformation into an artificial intelligence-focused business. Founder and CEO Thierry Ehrmann and family member Nadège Ehrmann have acquired additional shares in the company, with regulatory filings submitted to the French Financial Markets Authority. The family reaffirmed its confidence in the company's future and its substantial investments in developing proprietary AI solutions called "Intuitive Art Market" and "Blind Spot."

The company clarified that these share purchases are not part of a takeover bid or forced buyout, but rather demonstrate the family's commitment to supporting Artprice. Thierry Ehrmann has also completed an 1,800-page manuscript about artificial intelligence that includes 450 pages chronicling Artprice's history and its transformation. The English version of this work will be released in late August 2026 through various platforms, followed by a French edition in September.
Orgs: museum of contemporary art abode of chaos

stories.Headline: Dr. Dre Reveals His Use of AI Music as Artificial Intelligence Sparks Controversy
stories.Summary:
Dr. Dre has disclosed that he incorporates artificial intelligence into his music production process, sparking renewed debate about AI's role in the music industry. In an interview with collaborator Jimmy Iovine, Dre explained that he uses AI as a creative tool to explore possibilities with material he has already created, comparing it to earlier technologies like drum machines and synthesizers. He rejected the notion that AI threatens music, instead characterizing it as another production tool. Iovine suggested that other prominent producers, including Timbaland, are also using AI without publicly acknowledging it.

The revelation has intensified ongoing industry discussions about copyright, artist compensation, and whether AI constitutes a production aid or a creative replacement. Dre's comments have attracted criticism from some hip-hop fans who oppose AI's use in music, while streaming platforms like Spotify and Apple Music are developing ways to identify AI-generated content. The debate now centers on how the music industry will define and distinguish AI-assisted work from fully AI-generated material as the technology becomes increasingly prevalent in professional production.

stories.Headline: AIMX Singapore 2026 Accelerates AI Deployment Through Catalysing Industry Innovation and Advancing Global Collaborations
stories.Summary:
AIMX Singapore 2026 is a major international conference bringing together business leaders, policymakers, and technology innovators from more than 60 countries to discuss practical artificial intelligence deployment across industries. The event will be opened by Singapore's Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and will feature expert discussions on moving AI beyond pilot projects into full enterprise implementation. Key topics include human-centric AI leadership, autonomous systems, AI in healthcare workflows, and AI applications in ports and airports. The conference aims to position Singapore as a leading hub for responsible AI innovation while helping organizations overcome barriers to scaling AI initiatives across sectors like healthcare, robotics, logistics, transportation, and retail.

Beyond the conference program, AIMX Singapore 2026 will include an international exhibition featuring over 100 exhibitors, dedicated country pavilions from Hong Kong, Japan, and Singapore, and an AI Experience Zone with interactive demonstrations. Attendees can participate in business matching sessions through an event app, visit startup showcases, and access an Ecosystem Lounge for networking and workshops. The event is co-organized with TechInnovation and AI Gravity and aims to facilitate partnerships and commercialization opportunities. Registration is now open, with complimentary passes available for eligible industry professionals.

stories.Headline: Billionaires Stanley Druckenmiller and Dan Loeb Both Sold Broadcom and Piled Into This Virtual Monopoly Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Instead
stories.Summary:
Two prominent Wall Street investors, Stanley Druckenmiller and Dan Loeb, have made identical portfolio moves that signal shifting sentiment in the artificial intelligence sector. Both investors completely sold their Broadcom positions while simultaneously building stakes in Alphabet. Druckenmiller, a macro specialist who previously worked under George Soros, and Loeb, founder of the hedge fund Third Point, are known for their ability to rotate capital into emerging growth opportunities before consensus catches up. Their coordinated exit from Broadcom suggests they believe better risk-reward opportunities exist elsewhere in the AI ecosystem, despite Broadcom's central role in supplying components for AI data center infrastructure.

The investors' pivot toward Alphabet reflects confidence in the company's vertical integration strategy for artificial intelligence. Alphabet designs its own silicon called Tensor Processing Units, operates extensive data center and fiber networks, and develops AI models through its DeepMind lab under the Gemini family. The company leverages these capabilities across Google Search, YouTube, Android, and Workspace, creating what analysts describe as near-monopoly positioning in online search. Alphabet reported strong recent results with total revenue of 119.8 billion dollars, a 24 percent year-over-year increase, while Google Cloud revenue surged 82 percent to 24.8 billion dollars with a 514 billion dollar backlog.

stories.Headline: ADIB appoints Chief AI Officer as it advances Vision 2035
stories.Summary:
Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank has appointed Pedro Uria-Recio as its Chief AI Officer to drive artificial intelligence initiatives across the organization as part of its Vision 2035 strategy. Uria-Recio will oversee the responsible deployment of AI to enhance customer experiences, improve risk management, and boost operational efficiency while building necessary capabilities and infrastructure. He brings over 20 years of experience in technology and AI, previously serving as Chief Data and AI Officer at CIMB Bank in Malaysia, where he led AI strategy and deployment across Southeast Asia. He has also held senior roles at McKinsey, Axiata Group, and True Corporation.

ADIB's leadership views AI as a principal transformation enabler rather than merely a technology initiative, aiming to make banking simpler and more personalized for customers while strengthening decision-making processes. The bank currently serves 2.7 million customers and added 125,000 new customers in the first half of 2026. With over 94 percent of transactions conducted through digital channels, ADIB has established a strong digital banking foundation and is now investing in technology, data, AI, and talent to become the world's most innovative Islamic bank.

stories.Headline: Workers in China worry over being replaced as they adapt to the growing impact of AI on jobs
stories.Summary:
Chinese workers across multiple industries are increasingly concerned about job displacement as artificial intelligence technology becomes more widespread. Computer programmer Fei Zhaojun was laid off along with 160 colleagues after his boss questioned whether AI could replace human coders, a scenario becoming common as China's government actively encourages AI adoption through its "AI Plus" initiative. The use of AI has expanded rapidly into programming, translation, video production, and even physical tasks like parcel sorting, with 47.5% of Chinese industrial enterprises now using AI models compared to just 9.6% in 2024.

While some workers are adapting by using AI as a tool or starting new ventures, widespread job losses threaten economic stability. Women face particularly high displacement risk as they dominate automation-suitable fields like electronics assembly. China's economic growth is already slowing partly because consumers fear job loss and are spending less money. Though some experts suggest automation could eventually offset China's rapidly aging and shrinking workforce, immediate employment challenges remain serious, especially for young people aged 16 to 24.

stories.Headline: China's Inner Mongolia ramps up green computing, AI service exports
stories.Summary:
Inner Mongolia's autonomous region announced major expansion plans for its green computing and artificial intelligence industries at a conference in Hohhot on Saturday. Twelve projects valued at approximately 186.46 billion yuan, or 27.49 billion U.S. dollars, were signed at the event. The initiatives involve major companies including ByteDance's Volcano Engine, Cambricon Technologies, and China Telecom, and focus on developing intelligent computing centers, token factories, and manufacturing facilities for computing and electrical equipment.

Officials also launched construction on a new digital services platform designed to connect international developers with China's artificial intelligence models and green computing resources. The platform will assist Chinese artificial intelligence companies in expanding into overseas markets and provide services such as compliance assessment, computing-power distribution, and cross-border settlement. Inner Mongolia has become a major computing hub, with two regional areas operating computing capacity exceeding 300,000 petaflops combined, driven by the region's abundant wind and solar resources for powering data centers.

stories.Headline: Spanish scholar explores future of learning in the age of AI
stories.Summary:
Carles Sierra, a Spanish artificial intelligence researcher with four decades of experience, visited a school in Shantou, China to observe how AI is transforming education. At Keliyuan Experimental School, students use tablets with adaptive software that not only grades their work but identifies knowledge gaps and personalizes what each student learns next. Teachers can monitor study time, progress, and problem areas to provide targeted support. Sierra then traveled to Shanghai to meet Derek Haoyang Li, founder of Squirrel Ai Learning, the company behind this technology.

The adaptive platform breaks subjects into smaller learning objectives and uses diagnostic questions to tailor content to each student's needs. Rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach, students who progress quickly receive more challenging material while others can revisit foundational concepts. Sierra emphasizes that while AI can diagnose problems and personalize learning, it cannot replace human judgment, emotional support, or relationships essential to student growth. Teachers at the school confirmed AI assists rather than replaces their role in education.

stories.Headline: OpenAI wants California to strengthen its newly passed AI safety law
stories.Summary:
OpenAI is pushing California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety law the company helped pass in September 2025. The company wants new requirements for monitoring frontier AI models during training to detect potential security breaches or unauthorized access to confidential information. OpenAI is also calling for enhanced cybersecurity measures throughout the entire model development process to prevent AI systems from bypassing internal safeguards.

The existing law already includes substantial protections, requiring large AI developers to publish safety frameworks, establish incident reporting channels, protect whistleblowers, and allow the state Attorney General to impose civil penalties for noncompliance. OpenAI framed its requests as part of a broader "reverse federalism" strategy, suggesting that state-level standards could eventually become national policy while Congress remains inactive on federal AI legislation. The company emphasized this is a forward-looking effort to catch problems earlier rather than a response to specific incidents.

stories.Headline: Saudi-French AI ties deepen as Kingdom scales up digital economy
stories.Summary:
Saudi Arabia and France have significantly expanded their partnership in artificial intelligence and advanced technology over the past three years. Since 2023, when Saudi Communications and Information Technology Minister Abdullah Al-Swaha identified generative AI as a major cooperation opportunity, the two countries have broadened their collaboration to include large language models, robotics, quantum computing, space technology, and smart cities. A Strategic Partnership Council was established during French President Emmanuel Macron's December 2024 visit to Saudi Arabia, and subsequent meetings have involved discussions with major French AI companies and research institutions.

Saudi Arabia's digital economy has grown substantially to nearly $140 billion by February 2026, representing more than half of regional digital growth. The Kingdom's data center capacity expanded from less than 80 megawatts to over 440 megawatts, supporting AI development and deployment. France invested 127 billion dollars in AI infrastructure during 2025 to strengthen its global position. The partnership now encompasses researcher exchanges, joint laboratories, startup support, and cooperation on data governance and technology regulation, moving beyond investment discussions to concrete collaborative development efforts.

Articles.Title: Saudi-French AI ties deepen as Kingdom scales up digital economy
